concepts.def: The quantity you deliberately change in an experiment to investigate its effect.
The quantity you measure to see how it responds to changes in the independent variable.
A quantity kept constant throughout an experiment so it does not affect the outcome.
A reading error caused by viewing a scale at an angle rather than perpendicular to it.
Checking an instrument against a known standard and correcting for any offset it shows.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Practical Techniques — a core area of A-Level Physics.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Practical Techniques brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Practical Techniques.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: To avoid parallax error when reading a liquid level, you should:
options: Use a wider measuring cylinder.
Take the reading as quickly as possible.
Read the scale at eye level, perpendicular to it.
Read from above at 45 degrees.

mcqs.q: You vary the voltage across a lamp and measure the current. The dependent variable is:
options: The voltage
The temperature of the room
The length of the connecting leads
The current

mcqs.q: Why draw a line of best fit rather than joining the points dot-to-dot?
options: It makes the graph look longer.
It removes systematic error automatically.
Graphs are required to use curves only.
It averages out random scatter to reveal the underlying trend.

mcqs.q: A micrometer reads +0.04 mm with its jaws fully closed. You should:
options: Subtract 0.04 mm from each reading to correct the zero error.
Add 0.04 mm to each reading.
Ignore it because it is small.
Multiply every reading by 0.04.

mcqs.q: Should an anomalous point simply be included in the line of best fit?
options: No — identify it, repeat or investigate it, and exclude it from the fit if confirmed anomalous.
No — delete it secretly without comment.
Use a heavier pendulum bob.
Yes — every measured point must influence the line equally.

mcqs.q: How do you reduce the effect of reaction time when timing oscillations with a stopwatch?
options: Press the stopwatch buttons faster.
Time many oscillations and divide by the number of cycles to find one period.
No — gradients are read directly off the y-axis.
Use a heavier pendulum bob.

mcqs.q: Is the gradient of a graph found from two of your plotted data points?
options: No — use two widely separated points on the best-fit line itself.
No — gradients are read directly off the y-axis.
Yes — pick any two of your measured points.
No — delete it secretly without comment.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Dependent variable”?
options: A quantity kept constant throughout an experiment so it does not affect the outcome.
The quantity you measure to see how it responds to changes in the independent variable.
Checking an instrument against a known standard and correcting for any offset it shows.
The quantity you deliberately change in an experiment to investigate its effect.
